evidence.note: Explicit pass-boundary design up front (Lexer/Preprocessor/Type system/Codegen/Driver), with codegen planned as type-aware and SysV-ABI-aware including structs/varargs/floats — foresight targeting the hard features, not just trivial cases.
types.rs designed comprehensively at the outset (ptr/array/struct/union/enum/func/typedef), the representation that lets later features attach cleanly rather than forcing rewrites.
Clean module separation into token/preprocess/types/ast/parse/parse_init/codegen/main — well beyond ad-hoc string munging; distinct passes with distinct data structures.
Switch/case lowering added with only modest parse+codegen edits, showing the AST/codegen absorbed a mid-tier feature additively.
Complex and vector types (beyond the stated contract) added as new variants in types.rs — the type model proved extensible, features slotting in additively without wholesale rewrite.

Struct-by-value return ABI and nested functions required extensive codegen iteration, indicating the stack-machine codegen (no separate IR layer) did not fully anticipate every ABI detail — keeps this short of the top anchor.

reasoning: The agent established clean lexer/parser/sema/codegen separation and, crucially, designed a comprehensive type/layout model (struct/union/enum/ptr/array/typedef) up front, so structs, typedef, switch, and even out-of-contract features like complex and vector types slotted into types.rs additively without wholesale rewrites — the defining signature of anchor 8. It falls short of 10 because there is no distinct extensible IR (codegen is a stack machine off the AST) and genuinely hard ABI cases (struct-by-value returns, nested functions) demanded heavy codegen iteration rather than landing cleanly, so foresight was strong on data structures but incomplete on the codegen/ABI layer.
